findings.assertion: The decree creating the Sistema de Transporte Colectivo was signed 19 April and published 29 April 1967; construction ceremony followed on 19 June 1967. The later 1984 DOF decree explicitly refers back to the dated 1967 decree, but its full original legal text remains unexamined.
findings.period: Postwar urban infrastructure and metropolitan state
findings.source_locator: Gaceta UNAM 2019 HTML lines 11-13; DOF 1984 title lines 27-32
findings.limitations: The 1984 amendment is NOT the original 1967 decree. Exact 1967 powers and institutional structure cannot be published without original.

findings.assertion: Official STC chronology reports Line 1's Zaragoza–Chapultepec opening on 4 September 1969 with 12.660 km and 16 stations. This was a defined first section, not the present full Line 1 alignment.
findings.source_locator: STC indexed official chronology row '1 Zaragoza - Chapultepec'; Gaceta UNAM lines 6-13
findings.limitations: STC direct page unavailable (502); verify printed 1969 opening timetable and route maps before exact travel instructions.

findings.assertion: STC dates the first Line 2 Pino Suárez–Tasqueña section to 1 August 1970 and Tacuba–Pino Suárez expansion to 14 September 1970. Modern transfer connections must not be retrojected into 1969.
findings.source_locator: STC Línea 2 indexed official history row; STC chronology matching dates
findings.limitations: The full STC page could not be directly accessed; neither 1970 route map nor initial transfer architecture reviewed.

findings.assertion: Station pictograms were designed by a team including Lance Wyman, Arturo Quiñónez and Francisco Gallardo. The design sought immediate reference to nearby sites, historical figures or neighborhood identities and promoted legibility without relying on station name text.
findings.source_locator: Gaceta UNAM 2019 lines 22-26 quoting CDMX Metro; STC Línea 2 page indexed intellectual-property notice
findings.limitations: Original design briefs and attribution agreements unexamined; STC states iconography is protected by copyright; no image usage approved.

findings.assertion: A 2011 STC retrospective dates reserved women-and-children train-car arrangements to late 1970 following complaints about crowding; it also distinguishes later formalization in 2000 and an anti-harassment programme in 2007. These periods should not be compressed into one original policy.
findings.source_locator: STC press notice 12 Apr 2011 indexed lines beginning 'Durante el último bimestre de 1970' and 'A partir de julio del año 2000'
findings.limitations: Institutional retrospective only; original 1970 operational circulars, women's testimony and independent history not examined.

findings.assertion: Metro Insurgentes and the sunken Glorieta de los Insurgentes provide a physically legible late-1960s urban-design site. A 2014 UNAM history thesis specifically studies their modernizing urban discourse from 1967 to 1976, but its full findings have not yet been read.
findings.source_locator: UNAM thesis repository lines 7-20,38-73, title and provenance only
findings.limitations: Thesis metadata does NOT substantiate site-design details; original plans and current pedestrian access not checked.

findings.assertion: INAH identifies an in-situ pre-Hispanic structure dedicated to the wind god inside Pino Suárez station at José María Pino Suárez and José María Izazaga. Its presence in a working transfer station provides a concrete contrast between colonial/modern street grids and surviving Mexica fabric.
findings.source_locator: INAH Lugares lines 24-49; Secretaría de Cultura capsule lines 55-61
findings.limitations: INAH page hours are published listing, NOT verified live access; visitor signage/conditions and precise sightlines not inspected.

findings.assertion: An INAH account describes a larger ceremonial complex around José María Izazaga, with patios, stairways, other shrines, rooms, canals and a corridor associated with the Iztapalapa causeway. The retained Ehécatl shrine is one surviving element, not proof that the entire former complex remains visible.
findings.source_locator: Secretaría de Cultura capsule lines 55-58; Raúl Arana interview in El Universal 2017 lines 34-41
findings.limitations: Original excavation plans, chronology and topographic reconstruction missing; avoid precise ancient boundary or customs-post claims without primary verification.

findings.assertion: A 2017 rescue excavation reported fragments of Azteca III–IV pottery and remains approximately 35 m northeast of the Ehécatl shrine near Plaza Pino Suárez, provisionally related to Cuezcontitlan. This is a different 2017 excavation and must not be presented as another intact visible shrine today.
findings.period: Contemporary rescue archaeology and Mexica neighborhood
findings.source_locator: Animal Político 11 July 2017 lines 84-95 attributing statements to INAH archaeologist Donají Montero Guzmán
findings.limitations: Calpulli identification is an inference, not confirmed; 2017 excavation plan, context catalog and present visibility unknown.

findings.assertion: An article reproduces a report dated 28 September 1968 describing exposed superposed structures at Izazaga/Pino Suárez and archaeologists working amid active construction equipment, with potential threats to documentation and preservation. A 2017 interview with participant Raúl Arana independently recalls mechanical damage, but original logs and original 1968 issue are still needed.
findings.source_locator: El Universal 2021 article lines 31-49 reproducing 28 Sept 1968 coverage; Ventura 2017 lines 23-35
findings.limitations: 1968 press is excerpt mediated through 2021 reprint; original issue page scan, 1969 INAH Gussinyer report and construction logs must be checked. Discovery year 1967 vs excavations 1968 not reconciled.

findings.assertion: Doris Heyden's INAH paper abstract records a 93 cm sculpture found in September 1967 during Metro excavations, subsequently displayed in the Mexica hall of the National Museum of Anthropology and called 'Coatlicue'. It must not be identified as an object from the Pino Suárez Ehécatl shrine without a shared findspot inventory.
findings.source_locator: INAH Anales 7(2), 153–170, 1971 indexed journal abstract (PDF not examined)
findings.limitations: Only scholarly abstract inspected; findspot/location, original object catalog and iconographic debate unverified; do not confuse with the famous monumental Coatlicue.
